title: Separate successful buffered writes from final output delivery
applies_when: A program buffers output and reports success before deferred Flush or Close has delivered it, especially when small outputs succeed but larger outputs report a write error.
lesson: Trace the public entry through finalization and inspect how cleanup errors affect its returned status. A successful buffer Write does not prove delivery. Pair a directly failing writer with the same writer behind a small buffer, plus normal output and explicit flush controls. For a reviewed Linux CLI, /dev/full can expose ENOSPC without filling a disk; compare a short redirected write with one exceeding the buffer and inspect both exit status and stderr. GoAWK's pinned executeAll defers closeAll, which discards output-stream Close and output Flush errors. That source mechanism warrants a caller-level probe, not an automatic fatal-error patch.
avoid_when: Finalization policy may intentionally differ from explicit flush: GoAWK's current fflush test requires nonfatal diagnostics. Preserve prior interpreter errors, cancellation, child exit-status semantics and cleanup of all owned streams when proposing changes; do not close caller-owned streams to force a diagnostic. /dev/full is a Linux-specific control, not a portable dependency or GNU AWK oracle. Source evidence and selected reproductions do not establish maintainer intent, a qualified repair, full CI or improved Scout yield.

evidence.note: executeAll defers closeAll across normal and error returns. Source evidence for the finalization path, not an accepted change in its API contract.
closeAll discards stream-close and flusher errors. Explicit flushAll/flushWriter elsewhere log failures and return a boolean, which must not be conflated with final execution failure.
The accepted earlier fix ensures explicit flushing continues after a failed stream; it does not establish a final-close exit-status policy.
